newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian minister says gold exists in Busang.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian minister says gold exists in Busang.

text.p: Indonesia's Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana said on Wednesday there was gold at the Busang property in East Kalimantan province but the actual amount had yet to be ascertained.

Sudjana also said his ministry would hold a parliamentary hearing in June to discuss the fate of the applications for contracts of work by Canadian mining company Bre-X Minerals Ltd to further explore and develop the Busang find.
The applications have been put on hold by the government.
"We believe there is gold there. (But) whether the amount is 50 or 70 million ounces, we have yet to check it out," Sudjana told reporters.
Sudjana said he had seen local people panning for gold in East Kalimantan on Borneo island, and that geological maps also indicated that the area contained gold.
"People there earn their living through gold. We are waiting for the results of the due diligence process," he said.
Bre-X, which discovered the Busang deposit, said last Wednesday the property might hold less than the 71 million ounces of gold it had declared previously.
The original amount, worth some $25 billion at current gold prices, would make it the gold find of the century.
The stunning admission came a week after Bre-X chief geologist Michael de Guzman, who helped discover the deposit, fell out of a helicopter on his way to the Busang property.
The Philippine Embassy in Jakarta said on Wednesday it was waiting for an autopsy report on de Guzman.
"We have communicated with the national police to get a copy of the autopsy result," the embassy's third secretary and consul, Frank Simafranca, told Reuters.
He also described as understandable doubts expressed by de Guzman's brother that the geologist might have committed suicide as reported by some Indonesian officials.
A police spokesman said on Wednesday he had no information at the moment on the autopsy report and declined further comment.
De Guzman's brother, Simplicio, told Reuters in Manila on Tuesday he saw no reason why his brother would commit suicide.
Sudjana said there could have been mistakes in evaluating the amount of gold, but added that it should be the laboratory that should make a judgement. He did not elaborate.
Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc, which has a 15-percent stake in the Busang property, is carrying out an evaulation or due diligence at the property.
It said last Wednesday preliminary results of the drilling on Busang "indicate insignificant amounts of gold". Freeport's due diligence process is expected to be completed by end-April.

Sudjana was quoted by the official Antara news agency as saying in the East Kalimantan capital Samarinda on Tuesday that the government was waiting for the results of a study being carried out by a team which included government officials, Bre-X and Freeport.
